checkpoints.description: [1/1] Inference engines (ADR-155..163): assess every engine's token speed and version at the start of the device stage; ship llama.cpp through a pinned installer; let external engines (llama-server, Ollama, OpenAI-compatible servers) answer the tuner's items; tune on the fastest accurate engine and serve through it with an in-process fallback; one engine catalog with plugins; engine version tracking; crash recovery; cache-off serving. Recorded after the work was committed (bf2127e..b43b543).

impact_assessment.why: The user asked that tuning and serving use the best token-generation engine, assess each engine's speed, ship the engines, and make adding engines cheap.
impact_assessment.benefits: Measured on this machine: the tune picked llama-server on Vulkan (89 ms vs 205 ms per speed item) and serving was 386 tok/s against 149 in-process; four concurrent clients answered in 364 ms.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: a profile now names an engine and the app starts it, so loads can fail on another machine; dependency: a downloaded llama.cpp build and optional Ollama or attached servers; concurrency: an engine process per load, crash and restart paths; state: the profile records the engine and its build.
impact_assessment.mitigation: In-process fallback with a status notice; checksum-pinned installer; LlamaEngine refuses a load that names another engine; one guarded restart before any output; engine build recorded and compared on load; 1040 tests, tune:gate unchanged on all nine baselines, UI reviewed at 1440 and 390px; README, ADR-155..163 and docs/ENGINES.md updated.

handoff.next: serving through an attached OpenAI-compatible server needs a profile that can start it
handoff.open: CUDA, Metal and Ollama never ran on real hardware or servers here
